subject: general
question: A can do a work in 11 days and B can do the same work in 23 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(11, 23) = 253 units.

Efficiency: A = 23, B = 11. Combined Efficiency = 34 units/day.

Work done in 2 days = 34 × 2 = 68 units.

Work left = 253 − 68 = 185 units.

Fraction of work left = 185/253.

**∴ The correct answer is 185/253.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 11 days, Time taken by **B** = 23 days.

**Formula Used:** Work Done = Efficiency × Time | Fraction Left = 1 − (Work Done / Total Work)

⇒ Combined efficiency of **A and B** = 23 + 11 = 34 units/day

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 34 × 2 = 68 units

⇒ Remaining work = 253 − 68 = 185 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = 185 / 253

**∴ The correct answer is 185/253.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Fractional Work Method

If a person does work in 'n' days, work done in 1 day is 1/n. Work left after 'd' days is 1 − (d/n).

Combined Work Formula

If A takes 'x' days and B takes 'y' days, they together take (xy)/(x + y) days to finish the work.</p
